description: defk_upgrade takes over the defk_frame resource type (ERL_NIF_RT_TAKEOVER) but is untested. Risk: a frame suspended under the old NIF resumes into the new library's step function with a different frame layout. Test: reload the module while a kernel is mid-yield; decide whether to version frames or refuse the upgrade while frames are live.

comments.text:
Findings (OTP 29.0.3 / ERTS 17.0.3; source erl_nif.c, beam_bif_load.c, erl_nif docs at tag OTP-29.0.3). Experiment: start spin(4e8), suspend the caller between yields (:erlang.suspend_process), recompile the module with a different body and frame struct, resume.
(1) The feared crash cannot happen: the continuation is the OLD library's step_N function pointer. enif_schedule_nif bumps the calling library's dynlib_refc on first schedule (erl_nif.c ~396) and drops it when the NIF finally returns (nfunc_cleanup_nif_mod), so the old .so stays mapped and the kernel resumes in its own code with its own layout. Observed: old call returned the correct old-version result, new calls ran the new code.
(2) check_process_code counts a process with a pending scheduled NIF as running old code (erts_check_nfunc_in_area, beam_bif_load.c ~1172): soft_purge returns false, code:purge (or loading a third version) kills the caller. VM survives.
(3) The real bug was ERL_NIF_RT_TAKEOVER of the shared "defk_frame" type: the new library's dtor and frames_live counter applied to old frames. Observed new frames_live = -1 and old stuck at 1 after the old kernel finished or was killed. Harmless only while defk_ctx keeps its layout; with a padded defk_ctx in the new runtime the new dtor read past the old frame (UB, silent in that run).
Policy: per-image frame resource type ("defk_frame_<address of a static>"), no cross-library takeover. ERTS keeps a library loaded while instances of its resource types exist and destroys them with its own dtor (documented; erts_unload_nif/steal_resource_type). Upgrade uses CREATE|TAKEOVER, which only takes over when the same .so image is reloaded (same statics, same dtor). Refusing the upgrade was rejected: it would break every recompile while a kernel runs, and BEAM already keeps the old code alive correctly. After the fix: both counters return to 0, the old .so is unmapped (lsof) once its frames are gone and it is purged. Hot path untouched (load callbacks only), so no perf run.

title: Test hot code upgrade with suspended kernel frames
